item.title: NVIDIA Releases Open-Weight Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe for Multilingual Speech Tasks
item.description:
NVIDIA Releases Open-Weight Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe for Multilingual Speech Tasks

NVIDIA has open‑sourced Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a single checkpoint model that handles transcription, speaker attribution, translation, and audio question answering across many languages.

🔍 Overview

  • Open‑weight model available on Hugging Face and ModelScope.
  • Leads open‑weight rankings on the Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard (English) and on speaker‑attribution benchmarks.
  • Supports recordings up to one hour and up to eight simultaneous speakers.

🧩 How it Works

  • Architecture combines a speech encoder with a hybrid Mamba–Transformer mixture‑of‑experts language model.
  • Approximately 30 B total parameters, but only about 4 B are active per token, placing it on Artificial Analysis’s accuracy‑vs‑active‑parameter Pareto frontier.
  • Sortformer speaker cues are injected into the language model, enabling turn‑by‑turn speaker tagging during generation.
  • Word‑level timestamps are provided for all outputs.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Languages: Transcribes 40 languages, translates 31 languages to or from English, and performs speaker attribution in 13 languages.
  • Benchmark Performance:
    • English average WER: 5.33 % (first among open‑weight models, API models excluded).
    • Multilingual mean WER across seven languages: 4.62 % (lowest among evaluated open‑weight models).
    • Long‑form (up to one hour) mean WER: 10.98 % (lowest in the Open ASR comparison).
    • Speaker attribution: lowest diarization error on David AI’s 21‑language leaderboard and first place in VoiceArena’s 14‑system comparison.
    • AA‑WWER: 2.80 % with ~4 B active parameters, tying for first among open‑weight models.
    • On AA‑AgentTalk (voice‑agent set), WER 1.8 %, better than the next best open‑weight model (2.3 %).
  • Prompt‑Level Control: Users can guide output with natural‑language instructions, choose processing location, and adapt to domain vocabulary and accents.
  • Fine‑Tuning: Granary v2 multilingual data and NeMo Speech fine‑tuning tools let developers define target written forms and adapt the model to specific speech domains. In a medical case study, fine‑tuning reduced WER on held‑out speakers by 45.8 % relative to the best prompt.
  • Use‑Case Examples:
    • Captioning the 1940 film His Girl Friday with speaker labels, including overlapping dialogue.
    • Agora’s classroom demo: word‑level timestamps displayed alongside replay video, letting students see what was said and when.

🚀 Availability

  • Model checkpoint, Granary v2 data pipeline, and fine‑tuning recipes are publicly hosted on Hugging Face and ModelScope.
  • Quantized versions will be released soon, enabling local execution on RTX Spark, DGX Spark, Jetson AGX Thor, or scaling on Blackwell data‑center GPUs.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Provides a single open‑weight solution for multiple speech‑related tasks, reducing the need for separate models.
  • Sets new accuracy benchmarks for open‑weight speech systems while keeping active computational cost low.
  • Open data and fine‑tuning recipes empower developers to adapt the model to specialized domains such as medical transcription.
  • The upcoming quantized releases lower the barrier for edge deployment and private‑cloud use cases.

#NVIDIA #SpeechAI #OpenSource #Multilingual

Source: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2: Intelligent Multilingual Transcription You Can Prompt and Adapt

item.title: Apertus 1.5 Introduces Multimodal Pretraining, 262k Token Context and Thinking Mode
item.description:
Apertus 1.5 Introduces Multimodal Pretraining, 262k Token Context and Thinking Mode

Apertus 1.5 is a continued pretraining of the first‑generation model that adds large amounts of text and multimodal data while keeping the model fully open.

🔍 Overview

  • “Apertus 1.5 is a continued pretraining of the first generation model: adding 4 trillion tokens of text and multimodal training data to the 8B model and 2 trillion tokens to the 70B model, for a total of 19T and 17T, respectively.”
  • All releases are “fully open: open weights, open data, open values, and full training details.”
  • Native multimodal understanding: the models accept images and audio alongside text, “bringing documents, diagrams, and photos into the conversation.”
  • Spoken language is also processed, “though this remains experimental.”

🧩 How It Works

  • Multimodality is introduced in an early‑fusion manner: images and audio are tokenized and placed in the same sequence as text tokens, “instead of using a separate vision encoder.”
  • Image tokenization uses the Emu3.5 tokenizer (a 512×512 image → 1,024 tokens).
  • Audio tokenization uses WavTokenizer (40 tokens per second).
  • Only the vocabulary is extended, so “the architecture stays unchanged and training runs at text‑only speed.”
  • The models “understand images and audio but generate only text.”

⚙️ Key Details

  • Thinking Mode – “The models can be switched into a thinking mode to reason about the input before answering, which improves performance on reasoning problems.”
  • Long Context – Context window grows to 262,144 tokens, a 4× increase over Apertus 1.0.
  • Improved Instruction‑Following – Better instruction adherence than Apertus 1.0 gives more predictable and accurate responses.
  • Improved Tool Use – Trained for better tool integration, allowing more effective use of external tools and APIs.
  • Open Values – Stronger adherence to the Apertus Charter, providing transparency to the model’s values and principles.

📊 Training Pipeline

  • Pretraining Stages
    1. Unpaired: text plus standalone images and audio.
    2. Paired: image‑caption and audio‑transcript pairs.
    3. Cooldown: higher‑quality data with more math and code.
    4. Long Context: window grows step by step from 8k to 262k tokens.
  • More than half of the training tokens are text‑only, preserving the language abilities of Apertus 1.0.
  • Text data refreshed with sources such as FineWeb2‑HQ+, FinePDFs, and Nemotron‑CC.
  • All new data meets the same bar as before: publicly available, permissively licensed, and with robots.txt opt‑outs respected retroactively. Every source is listed in apertus‑data‑transparency.
  • Post‑training stages: SFT → long‑context SFT → RL → DPO → charter alignment (SDPO).
    • SFT on 3.7M text samples plus image and speech data.
    • Reasoning traces added only to prompts the model can’t already solve without them.
    • Tool‑use data restricted to execution‑verified trajectories.
    • Long‑context SFT at the full 262k window restores the long‑context ability that short‑context SFT erodes.
    • RL with verifiable rewards (RLVR) on about 350k math, code, instruction‑following, multilingual, and vision prompts, mixing thinking on and off.
    • DPO with judge‑scored preference pairs improves chat quality, tool use, and safety.
  • The text SFT mix, the preference pool, and the training pairs are released on Hugging Face.

🚀 Availability

  • All weights, data, values, and full training details are released openly.
  • The released assets include the text SFT mix and the preference pool used for DPO.

#Apertus #MultimodalAI #OpenSource #LongContext

Source: Apertus 1.5 Release Notes

item.title: Reflection AI releases open‑weight model Beam with 5 trillion parameters
item.description:
Reflection AI releases open‑weight model Beam with 5 trillion parameters

Reflection AI announced its first open‑weight base model, Beam, on 5 October 2026 (U.S. time).

🔍 Overview

  • Beam is the inaugural open‑weight model from the NVIDIA‑backed U.S. AI startup Reflection AI.
  • The release came more than six months later than the company’s original target of early 2026.
  • At the time of launch the company’s valuation had risen from $8 billion to $250 billion pre‑money, despite the model not having been released earlier.
  • In the global landscape, Chinese models such as DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3, GLM‑5.3 and Qwen 3.8‑Max dominate the open‑weight segment, while U.S. closed‑model leaders remain OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.

🧩 How it works

  • Beam uses a Sparse Mixture‑of‑Experts (MoE) architecture. Although the total parameter count is 5 010 billion, only 230 billion active parameters are used per token.
  • Pre‑training consumed 23.8 trillion tokens.
  • Training relied on NVIDIA GB300 hardware: 6 144 units for pre‑training and 10 500 units for reinforcement learning (RL) over four weeks, generating over 100 million rollouts.
  • Scoring and learning were performed on a sandbox of approximately 1.3 billion entries, with nearly 1 million RL environments prepared.

⚙️ Key details

Attribute Value
Total parameters 5 010 billion
Active parameters per token 230 billion
Pre‑training data 23.8 trillion tokens
Pre‑training compute 6 144 NVIDIA GB300 units
RL compute 10 500 NVIDIA GB300 units (4 weeks)
Rollouts generated >100 million
Sandbox size ~1.3 billion
RL environments prepared ~1 million

💡 Why it matters

  • Beam offers inference quality comparable to GLM‑5.2 while requiring one‑quarter to one‑third of the inference compute thanks to its 23 billion‑active‑parameter design.
  • The model does not claim superiority over current Chinese top models; the company itself notes that models such as Kimi K3 still lead in raw capability.
  • Reflection AI’s broader goal is to provide an “AI Factory” that lets enterprises and governments train proprietary agents using their own data and GPU resources, rather than selling the model itself.
  • The startup was founded in March 2024, is based in Brooklyn, NY, and is expanding hiring across New York, San Francisco, London and Washington DC.
  • Founders Misha Laskin (CEO) and Ioannis Antonoglou (CTO), both former Google DeepMind staff, initially positioned the company around Autonomous Coding – AI that can independently understand, design, modify, test and improve software.
  • In June 2026, during London Tech Week, UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced Reflection’s UK expansion plan: over 100 high‑skill hires in the next 12 months and a target of more than 1 000 employees in the UK within three years.

#ReflectionAI #OpenWeight #MoE #AIFactory #AutonomousCoding

Source: NVIDIAが賭ける「米国版DeepSeek」―Reflection AI初の自社オープンウェイト基盤モデル「Beam」の衝撃｜香川友志

item.title: EmbeddingGemma 2 released under Apache 2.0 license
item.description:
EmbeddingGemma 2 released under Apache 2.0 license

EmbeddingGemma 2, an embedding model, was announced on 6 October 2026 and is licensed under Apache 2.0.

🔍 Overview

  • The model is designed for generating embedding vectors, which are commonly calculated in the thousands or millions and stored for later similarity comparison.
  • Its open‑source Apache 2.0 license means the weights are publicly available for anyone to download and run.

💡 Why it matters

  • Embedding models are often used at scale, so relying on a closed, proprietary, hosted‑only model can create vendor lock‑in risk.
  • If a provider stops offering a proprietary model, users may have to re‑embed all stored vectors, incurring additional cost.
  • An open‑license model lets users switch providers or self‑host later, avoiding that risk.

⚙️ Key details

  • License: Apache 2.0 (open source, permissive).
  • Target use‑case: Large‑scale embedding generation where millions of vectors are stored for later comparison.
  • User preference expressed: Pay a provider for hosted inference while retaining the ability to run the open‑weights version themselves if hosting ends.

🚀 Availability

  • The model’s weights are publicly available under the Apache 2.0 license, allowing anyone to download and run the model independently.
  • Users can still choose a hosted service for convenience, knowing they have a fallback option.

No additional figures are provided.

#EmbeddingGemma #OpenSource #AIEmbeddings #ApacheLicense

Source: Comment: EmbeddingGemma 2

item.title: Aleph Alpha Releases Kolibri Open-Weight Bilingual Model for Sovereign Operations
item.description:
Aleph Alpha Releases Kolibri Open-Weight Bilingual Model for Sovereign Operations

Aleph Alpha has released Kolibri, an open-weight bilingual Mixture-of-Experts model designed for sovereign, mission-critical work in government and regulated industries. Building on the earlier Kolibri Origin and the company’s automated Model Factory, this new development is optimized for English and German and supports on-premises deployment to protect internal data.

🔍 Overview

  • Bilingual Focus: Optimized for English and German, with German accounting for 21.3% of pre-training tokens.
  • Open Access: Full weights available on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license.
  • Target Industries: Specialized for public administration, automotive, semiconductors, industrial technology, and aerospace.
  • Deployment: Customers can run the model on-premises to avoid sending internal data to third-party services.

🧩 How it works

Kolibri utilizes a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Transformer architecture and a unique attention mechanism to balance performance with inference costs.

  • Parameters: 78.1 billion total parameters, with 3.46 billion active per token.
  • Expert Structure: 384 experts with six active per token.
  • Attention Layers: Full attention is used in 10 of 50 layers, while the remaining 40 use a 512-token sliding window.
  • Training: Developed in Germany and trained in Germany and Finland on 768 B200 GPUs. It was trained on nearly 24 trillion tokens over a 21-day initial period followed by mid-training and long-context adaptation.
  • Grounding: Trained using the Merlin-Arthur procedure and abstention examples, teaching the model to withhold answers when evidence is absent.

⚙️ Key details

Category Metric / Feature
Context Support Up to 1,048,576 tokens
English Overall Score 75.5
German Overall Score 70.8
AIME 2025 96.9
LiveCodeBench v6 85.9
BFCL v4 Overall 61.4
Vocabulary 128,000-entry bilingual vocabulary designed to preserve German compounds
Reasoning Settings Four options: none, low, medium, and high

🚀 Availability

Kolibri is available for download on Hugging Face. For deployment, Aleph Alpha provides an inference package and a Kolibri-specific vLLM plugin, along with documented reasoning and tool-call parsers.

💡 Why it matters

Aleph Alpha states that Kolibri sits on the quality-versus-serving-cost Pareto frontier in both English and German. It is designed to match models with up to four times as many active parameters on math, code, grounding, and agentic tasks. By controlling the data curation, training, and evaluation within Europe, the model is intended to meet strict European compliance and sovereignty requirements.

#AlephAlpha #Kolibri #OpenWeight #BilingualAI #AISovereignty

Source: Aleph Alpha releases open-weight Kolibri with 1M context

item.title: Qwen3.8 Max Leads September 2026 Open‑Weight LLM Ranking
item.description:
Qwen3.8 Max Leads September 2026 Open‑Weight LLM Ranking

The latest open‑weight benchmark shows Qwen3.8 Max as the top‑scoring open‑source large language model.

🔎 Overview

  • Qwen3.8 Max is the best open‑source LLM by current open‑weight benchmark score.
  • It leads the September 2026 open‑weight ranking with a BenchAlign v5 score of 71.6.
  • The ranking includes 104 models and uses the public BenchAlign v5 overall lane filtered to downloadable weights.

📈 Ranking Details

Model Score Evidence
Qwen3.8 Max (Alibaba) 71.6 Supported
GLM-5.3 68.4 Estimated
GLM-5.2 68.1 Supported
  • The open‑weight slice starts with Qwen3.8 Max, followed by GLM‑5.3 and GLM‑5.2.
  • Scores compare measured capability and do not decide licensing permissiveness, hardware fit, or cost of self‑hosting versus API use.
  • Supported and Estimated describe the evidence behind each position; they are not separate leaderboards.

⚙️ Technical Context

  • Open‑weight models are ranked by the same public BenchAlign v5 overall score as proprietary models.
  • The live table recomputes from the public BenchAlign v5 artifact.
  • MiniMax M3 led a July 14 snapshot, showing that rankings can change over time.

📚 Licensing & Deployment

  • Every ranked model publishes downloadable weights, but not every license is OSI‑approved.
  • The license directory separates OSI‑approved licenses from community terms.
  • A smaller deployment directory lists models with a self‑host catalog record, keeping license and hardware claims auditable.
  • A missing row in that directory means the deployment catalog is incomplete, not that the model cannot be self‑hosted.

🌐 Why it matters

  • The current top tier is dominated by Chinese labs (DeepSeek, Zhipu/GLM, Moonshot/Kimi, Alibaba/Qwen, MiniMax) with Meta and Mistral behind on the live ranking.
  • Open‑weight ranking provides a transparent view of model capability independent of proprietary offerings.

#OpenWeight #LLM #BenchAlign #AIranking

Source: Open-Source LLM Leaderboard 2026: 104 Models Ranked
